paper.title: Accurate piezoelectric tensor prediction with equivariant attention tensor graph neural network
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) to predict the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor for both bulk and two-dimensional materials, leveraging irreducible decomposition to preserve crystal symmetry and frame independence. It validates the model on datasets from Materials Project, C2DB, and high-throughput DFT studies, then uses it to screen for new high-performance piezoelectric candidates, which are experimentally validated via DFPT calculations.

task.objective: accurately predict the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor for crystalline materials
constraints: must be independent of reference frame
must satisfy index symmetry eijk = eikj
output_goal: full third-rank piezoelectric tensor in Voigt notation (3×6 matrix)

evidence.text: we propose an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) that can identify crystal symmetry and remain independent of the reference frame, ultimately enabling the accurate prediction of the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor.

EATGNN can establish the relationship between crystal structures and their properties... Ultimately, the model outputs the piezoelectric tensor in its irreducible representation, which is then post-processed to obtain the target piezoelectric tensor.

stages.stage_name_raw: acquisition of piezoelectric tensor data from computational databases
stages.stage_goal: obtain labeled piezoelectric tensor data for training and testing
stage_input: high-throughput computational study on piezoelectric tensors
stage_output: dataset of piezoelectric tensors for bulk and 2D materials

evidence.text: The piezoelectric tensor data of bulk crystals in this work was obtained from the Materials Project21 and a recent high-throughput computational study on piezoelectric tensors24,30.
The piezoelectric tensor data of 2D materials was obtained from the C2DB database33,34, comprising a total of 1382 data points...

stages.stage_goal: clean dataset by removing outliers and enforcing crystallographic symmetry constraints on tensor labels

evidence.text: Due to the presence of a signiﬁcant number of outliers in the piezoelectric tensors, we performed data resampling before applying machine learning techniques to prevent overﬁtting.

We examined all materials dataset to ensure that the target piezoelectric tensors are consistent with the material’s symmetry. Furthermore, we mathematically adjusted those piezoelectric tensors that did not conform to the material’s symmetry to be invariant under crystallographic symmetry operations.

We ﬁrst checked whether the piezoelectric tensors in the dataset satisfy the symmetry of their corresponding crystal structures. This was achieved by applying the crystal structure’s symmetry operations to the tensor and checking if it remains invariant under these operations. If a change occurred, we transformed the tensor into a symmetry-compliant form that respects the lattice symmetry.

stages.stage_name_raw: training EATGNN on piezoelectric tensor data
stages.stage_goal: optimize EATGNN parameters to minimize prediction error on piezoelectric tensor components

evidence.text: Networks are trained using a mean-squared-error loss function based on complete piezoelectric tensor: loss = 1/N Σ Σ (e′_nijk − e_nijk)² / 27
We train this model with the AdamW optimizer to minimize the loss function with a mini-batch size of 16.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluation of EATGNN performance on test sets
stages.stage_goal: quantify prediction accuracy using MAE and RMSE metrics on held-out test data
stage_output: MAE and RMSE scores for bulk and 2D materials

evidence.text: The RMSE and MAE of EATGNN on the test set are 0.154 C/m2 and 0.141 C/m2, respectively.
the RMSE and MAE of our model are 50.6 pC/m and 16.8 pC/m, respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: screening bulk and 2D materials databases for high-piezoelectric candidates
stages.stage_goal: generate candidate materials predicted to have large piezoelectric response
stage_output: list of candidate materials with predicted large |e_ij|_max

evidence.text: In order to discover new potential high-performance piezoelectric materials, we use our model on both 3D and 2D materials in the Materials Project and 2DMatPedia database36, respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: applying physical filters to candidate list
stages.stage_goal: filter candidates using domain-specific criteria to retain only physically viable materials
stage_output: filtered candidate list satisfying inversion asymmetry, bandgap > 0.1 eV, etc.

evidence.text: Our selection criteria are 1) out of the training datasets, 2) inversion asymmetry, 3) Egap > 0.1 eV, and 4) Nuc < 30 atoms.

stages.stage_goal: verify predicted piezoelectric tensors using first-principles calculations

evidence.text: Using our model, we identify several good candidates (See in Tables 3 and 4 and Supplementary Material), which are further validated using density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) calculations.
